title: Agreement with the affine Picard functor of file 06
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a
smooth projective curve over
$k$ which is geometrically integral over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The restriction of
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ to affine $k$-schemes
$T=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is canonically the sheafification presented in
[def-sc-picard-functor], namely the fppf sheafification of
$R\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(X\times_k\operatorname{Spec} R)$;
more precisely
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}(\operatorname{Spec}(R))=\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}^{\mathrm{sc}}(R)$ where
the right side is the value of the functor of [def-sc-picard-functor].

proof.text: On an affine k-scheme T = Spec(R), the big-site Picard presheaf and the affine-site presheaf both send T to Pic(X ×_k T), with identical pullback maps, by def-pc-picard-presheaf. Thus their restrictions are the same presheaf.

For the Picard presheaf, lem-pc-fppf-affine-sheafification-restriction gives a canonical and functorial identification of the restriction of its big-site fppf sheafification to affine objects with the fppf sheafification of its restriction to the affine site.

By def-pc-picard-functor, the left-hand sheaf is Pic_{X/k}; by def-sc-picard-functor, the affine-site sheafification of the common presheaf is Pic_{X/k}^{sc}. Evaluating the canonical identification from the preceding step at T = Spec(R) yields Pic_{X/k}(Spec(R)) = Pic_{X/k}^{sc}(R), naturally in affine k-schemes.
